section: two units of work: a request, or a program
text: A YAML file says how to render each document into text, the harness builds every request up front (context plus what to compute: a log-probability or a generation with stop strings), sends them in batches to a backend that only knows three methods, and then runs filters and metrics over the responses.

section: how each scores: three decisions inside every number
text: Probabilities or text lm-eval-harness has four request types ( lm_eval/api/instance.py ), and a backend only has to implement three methods to run all of them ( model guide ): loglikelihood(context, continuation) : the log-probability of a given continuation and whether it is the greedy one.
label: core
key: implements three methods to run them all

section: how each scores: three decisions inside every number
text: A multiple_choice task asks it once per option and picks the largest.
label: core
key: asks it once per option and picks the largest

section: how each scores: three decisions inside every number
text: No sampling, deterministic, cheap, works on base models; it measures how the model ranks given options, never whether it can produce an answer, and it needs log-probabilities of the prompt, which most chat APIs do not return. loglikelihood_rolling(text) : the log-probability of a whole text, for perplexity and bits-per-byte. generate_until(context, until=[...]) : generate until a stop string, then post-process with filters.
label: core
key: it needs prompt log-probabilities, which most chat APIs do not return

section: how each scores: three decisions inside every number
text: This is what chat and reasoning models need, and every extraction rule becomes part of the score.
label: core
key: every extraction rule becomes part of the score

section: how each scores: three decisions inside every number
text: Length normalisation, exactly For multiple_choice tasks lm-eval reports acc (argmax of the summed log-probabilities), acc_norm (argmax of the sum divided by the option's length in characters ), and, when asked, acc_bytes (divided by its UTF-8 byte length) and acc_mutual_info ( task.py lines 1494 to 1560 ).
label: core

section: how each scores: three decisions inside every number
text: The old version of this page called acc_norm byte-length normalised; it is character-length, which is the same for ASCII options and different for most other scripts.
label: core
key: it is character-length, the same for ASCII options

text: On GSM8K, the same benchmark in each harness uses a different rule (the tab One task, every harness runs all of them on real outputs): Harness Rule for the GSM8K answer lm-eval gsm8k Two filters reported side by side: strict-match needs #### <number> (the training-set format the 5 shots teach); flexible-extract takes the last number-like string.
label: core

section: how each scores: three decisions inside every number
text: Then exact_match after removing commas, $ and a trailing period inspect_evals gsm8k The prompt asks for ANSWER: $ANSWER , but the scorer match(numeric=True) ignores that line: it takes the last number in the whole output and compares numerically, formatted to 5 significant digits ( .5g ): for the 18 of 1,319 test answers above 99,999, a prediction of 114,201 matches a gold of 114,200 lighteval gsm8k Parses expressions and LaTeX (a boxed answer first) from the output and the gold, then compares the parsed values HELM gsm final_number_exact_match : the last match of -?[\d,]+(?:.\d+)? in output and gold.
label: core
key: a prediction of 114,201 matches a gold of 114,200

text: A Task is a dataset, a solver and a scorer.
label: core

text: A solver transforms a TaskState (messages, output, a per-sample store); solvers compose into chains: system_message() , prompt_template() , generate() , chain_of_thought() , self_critique() , multiple_choice() , use_tools() , or a whole agent such as react() (the older basic_agent() still ships).
label: depth

text: A scorer grades the final state: exact() , match() , includes() , pattern() , choice() , answer() , math() , model_graded_qa() , model_graded_fact() , the perplexity scorers, or custom Python, including batteries of judges.
label: depth

text: Metrics aggregate scores ( accuracy , stderr , bootstrap_stderr , ci_wilson , even krippendorff_alpha ); Epochs reruns each sample and reduces with mean, median, mode, max, at_least_k or pass_at_k ( scorer exports ).
